criteria_results.title: §2(a): Restore 'entitlement order' language
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s instruction-only language and restores “Entitlement Orders” in the relevant control provision, while also directing restoration of the defined term and conforming references. This is consistent with the UCC Article 8 control framework.

criteria_results.title: Cover note explains §2(a) entitlement order position
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the entitlement-order change, states that Pinnacle rejects the Bank's substitution and restores “Entitlement Order” references, and explains the UCC Article 8 rationale: preserving control if an account is characterized as a securities account and avoiding ambiguity in the control arrangement.

criteria_results.title: §2(b): Address springing exclusive control and reject broad Bank carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline retains springing exclusive control triggered by the Bank’s receipt and authentication of an NOEC, while expressly ending Graycliff’s operating rights at that point. It requires the Bank to cease following Depositor instructions, reject new Depositor debits, withdrawals, and transfers, and comply exclusively with the Secured Party’s instructions and entitlement orders. Thus, it rejects the broad post-NOEC operating carve-out.

criteria_results.title: §3: Reject Bank set-off priority over Secured Party instructions
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s proposed priority for set-off, recoupment, liens, and security interests. It restores a waterfall under which, after receipt of an NOEC, the Bank must follow the Secured Party’s instructions exclusively, with any set-off rights limited to expressly permitted exceptions.

criteria_results.title: §4: Narrow expanded self-help set-off to direct, liquidated obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s broad “any obligation…whether direct or contingent” formulation and limits set-off to obligations that are direct, matured, liquidated, due and payable, and arise under the deposit-account agreements. It also excludes contingent, disputed, unliquidated, derivative, affiliate, and unrelated obligations, thereby narrowing set-off to account-related fees and charges.

criteria_results.title: §5: Propose 3-business-day NOEC compliance period
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s five-business-day period and proposes in Section 5.2 that compliance begin no later than the third Business Day after receipt and authentication of the NOEC. It does not restore the original two-business-day period.

criteria_results.title: §6: Reject indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects indemnification for the Bank’s own gross negligence and adds a carve-out excluding losses resulting from the Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud (as well as material breach). This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §7(a): Reject $50,000 aggregate liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects and deletes the $50,000 aggregate liability cap, replacing it with language stating that the Bank's liability is not subject to an aggregate dollar cap. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §7(b): Address mutual consequential/punitive/indirect damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly addresses the mutual consequential, punitive, indirect, special, and exemplary damages waiver in Issue 8. It accepts the waiver in principle while qualifying it so it does not limit indemnification, direct damages, or losses arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach.

criteria_results.title: Cover note confirms position on §7(b) mutual damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the mutual consequential, special, punitive, and exemplary damages waiver under the heading “Consequential damages waiver — accept in principle, subject to clarification.” It confirms acceptance while qualifying that the waiver must not limit indemnification, direct damages, or liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach.

criteria_results.title: §8: Reject 90-day lookback; propose full subordination or 180-day lookback
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s 90-day lookback and proposes full subordination as Pinnacle’s preferred position, with a 180-day lookback as the minimum fallback. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §9: Reject 30-day unilateral termination; propose 90-day notice with transition rights
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s unilateral 30-day termination right and replaces it with at least 90 days’ prior written notice plus transition protections. The agreement remains effective until replacement accounts and a replacement control agreement are established and the Secured Party confirms completion in writing, while the Bank must continue performing during the notice period.

criteria_results.title: §10: Restore New York governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects North Carolina governing law in Section 10.1 and restores New York governing law and New York jurisdiction.

criteria_results.title: Cover note acknowledges New York governing law is strongly preferred with possible flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly rejects North Carolina law and states that New York law and courts should be restored because New York governs the Credit Agreement and is the appropriate framework. This clearly indicates a strong preference for New York, even though it does not expressly offer flexibility if that position is a deal-breaker.

criteria_results.title: §12: Restore no-prior-control-agreement representation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s deletion in §12.1(b) and reinstates a knowledge-qualified representation that the Bank has not entered into another control agreement and has no written notice or actual knowledge of any competing lien or adverse claim on the accounts.

criteria_results.title: §13: Restore successor-bank notification obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank's deletion and reinstates a successor-bank notification obligation in Section 9.1, requiring at least 30 days' prior written notice to the Secured Party of a proposed transfer of the Accounts or other succession, subject to limited legal or practicability exceptions.

criteria_results.title: §11: Accept annual maintenance fee but negotiate down $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly accepts the $3,500 annual maintenance fee per account ($10,500 total) and negotiates the $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement down to the lesser of $7,500 or the Bank’s actual, reasonable, documented outside-counsel fees.

criteria_results.title: ACA maintains form and substance satisfactory to Administrative Agent
criteria_results.reasoning: The counter-redline preserves the essential UCC control mechanics: it restores Entitlement Order terminology where Article 8 may apply, permits ordinary-course operation only before an NOEC, requires cessation of new Depositor instructions upon NOEC receipt, and gives the Secured Party exclusive post-NOEC instruction authority. It also rejects unrestricted Bank set-off priority and limits any set-off to narrow, matured account-level obligations. The authentication and implementation period does not eliminate control because the Accounts are frozen against new Depositor activity during that period.

criteria_results.title: Cover note maintains professional and cordial tone
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note is professional, courteous, and appropriate for inter-counsel negotiations. It thanks opposing counsel, explains Pinnacle’s positions clearly and firmly without inflammatory language, identifies practical compromises, invites further discussion, and closes with a courteous request tied to the transaction deadline.
